title: Equilibrium Language Models
claim: Our compressed model matches the dense model across all benchmarks, while competing pruning baselines lose accuracy, especially on reasoning and code tasks.
layout: 1 radar chart, legend on top, benchmarks around the axes, ours outlined in red
description: A single radar (spider) chart compares six methods on eight benchmarks: SIQA, PIQA, MBPP, HumanEval, MATH, GSM8K, MMLU and OBQA. A legend across the top names Dense LLMs (dashed pink), ELM (solid red/orange), Shortened-LLaMA (green), ReplaceMe (gray), LLM-Streamline (blue) and Sheared-LLaMA (gold). Radial rings are labeled 25%, 50%, 75% and 100%. The ELM polygon, filled with translucent pink, sits almost exactly on the outer rim and overlaps the dense dashed line. The baselines shrink inward, with the largest drops on MATH, GSM8K and HumanEval. ReplaceMe collapses toward the center on several axes. The eye goes first to the large pink outer shape, then to the shrunken inner polygons. Axis labels use a playful handwritten-style font.
caption: Benchmark evaluation of pruning baselines on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) excel across diverse applications but remain impractical for edge deployment due to severe memory bottlenecks at the edge devices. We propose Equilibrium Language Models (ELMs), a novel compression framework that replaces groups of Transformer layers with a lightweight fixed-point network, reinterpreting deep computation as solving for an equilibrium state. To achieve ELMs, We introduce Group Pruning Policy Optimization , which automatically learns optimal pruning intervals. Moreover, we propose One-Step KV-Cache , which drastically reduces memory overhead by storing only the final iteration cache without compromising the accuracy, to enable effective deployment at the edge devices. Across different tasks such as common sense reasoning, mathematical problem solving, and code generation, ELMs prune 28\% of parameters while retaining 99\% of the accuracy of dense fine-tuned LLMs, establishing a new direction for memory-efficient edge deployment of large models.
